The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. stories.summary: Nigeria Daily - Why Does Farmer-Herder Violence Keep Returning? 20 October 2026 Daily Trust (Abuja) By Luqman Awwal Agono Farmer-herder clashes remain a major security and agricultural challenge in Nigeria, threatening lives, destroying livelihoods and raising concerns about food production. Despite years of government interventions, including the National Livestock Transformation Plan, RUGA settlements and renewed efforts to promote ranching, violence continues to recur in affected communities. The latest violence in Paikon-Kore, Gwagwalada Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory, has renewed questions about why these clashes persist, the effectiveness of government interventions, and the challenges of finding a lasting solution to disputes over farmland, grazing routes and access to water. Today on Nigeria Daily, we examine why farmer-herder clashes keep recurring despite government efforts, what has prevented ranching from becoming a widely adopted solution, and what needs to change to restore peace and prevent further violence. Mr Abdul-Wahab, the appellant, wants the Court of Appeal to overturn the trial High Court's decision of July 18 that rejected his claim that the charge sheet was defective and unfit for the trial. In the ruling, the trial High Court judge, Justice Francis Achibonga, said there was sufficient information to enable the defence to conduct proceedings against the accused, who is standing trial together with his wife, Faiza Seidu Wuni, for allegedly causing financial loss of GH¢78 million to the state. His lawyers, led by Mr Godfred Yeboah Dame, a former Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, urged the Court of Appeal to quash the entire charges. Moving the application, Mr Dame told the three-member panel of judges, presided over by Justice Noble Nkrumah, that his client's right to a fair trial would be affected if the defective charges were not quashed.

stories.title: Fleeing the frontline: Yemeni families cross Red Sea to Djibouti as Houthi conflict rages
stories.summary: Madinah Abdullah (in pink) and her family members at the Markazi humanitarian site in Obock, Djibouti, on 6 October. Photograph: Carlos Mureithi/The Guardian Their overland routes to safety blocked off, several thousand people have boarded boats to escape gunfire, bombing and a dire humanitarian situation By Carlos Mureithi in Obock A bubaker Saeed was fishing in the Red Sea off Yemen’s coast last month when he noticed explosions in the distance. His mind turned immediately to his wife and two children, and he raced back to his home village of al-Wahijah. Aircraft from the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemeni government forces had launched airstrikes in surrounding areas, targeting members of the Iran-aligned Houthi militia as its fighters approached the nearby port city of Mocha. “They were bombing Houthis while Houthis were 1km away from us,” the 50-year-old recalled. By the time he reached the shore, the rebels had arrived and were battling government forces on the ground.

stories.summary: MDB Heads Strengthen Joint Action in Manila to Deliver More Financing and Greater Impact 17 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) The Heads of Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) Group met at the Asian Development Bank (ADB) headquarters in Manila today to discuss how to deliver more financing and greater impact to support developing members as they face mounting challenges. It was the Group's first-ever meeting in the Philippines, hosted by ADB as its 2026 Chair. "Conflict, economic uncertainty, high debt, inflation and disasters are placing growing pressure on our members and making development harder," said ADB President Masato Kanda, host and current Chair of the MDB Heads Group . "Our meeting in Manila was an opportunity to turn shared commitments into practical action, so we can help members protect their development gains, attract investment, and build more resilient economies." Against a backdrop of disasters, conflicts, difficult macroeconomic conditions, and constrained fiscal space, the Heads reaffirmed MDBs' readiness to provide timely financial and analytical support to protect vulnerable populations and sustain investment in jobs and resilient long-term growth. In a joint statement, the Heads welcomed the significant progress achieved this year working as a system to mobilize private capital, and on joint actions to advance jobs, nature, climate, water, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and other common development priorities, and on efforts to enhance system efficiency for greater impact at scale, in line with each institution's mandate, strategy and operational model. The role of Chair of the Heads of MDBs Group will be passed in December from ADB to the European Investment Bank Group. The Heads of MDBs Group includes the African Development Bank Group, Asian Development Bank, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Council of Europe Development Bank, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, European Investment Bank Group, Inter-American Development Bank Group, Islamic Development Bank, New Development Bank, and the World Bank Group.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda, Nigeria Army Chiefs Discuss Training, Skills Exchanges
stories.summary: Rwanda, Nigeria Army Chiefs Discuss Training, Skills Exchanges Nigerian Army/Facebook Rwanda, Nigeria army chiefs discuss training, skills exchanges. 19 October 2026 The New Times (Kigali) By Jesca Mutamba Nigeria's Chief of Army Staff, Lt Gen Waidi Shaibu, arrived in Rwanda on Sunday, October 18, for a five-day official visit aimed at strengthening defence cooperation between the two countries. On Monday, Shaibu visited Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) Headquarters in Kigali, where he paid a courtesy call on Chief of Defence Staff Gen Mubarakh Muganga and held bilateral talks with RDF Army Chief of Staff Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi. Shaibu said the two sides had committed to implementing existing memoranda of understanding covering military training, the exchange of directing staff and logistics personnel. "As the outcome of today's discussion, we have made key promises to implement the various memoranda of understanding that have been there between both countries in the area of training, exchange of directing staff as well as logisticians," he said. The discussions also covered defence and security developments of mutual interest to the two countries. Shaibu arrived in Rwanda on October 18 along with his delegation and are scheduled to conclude their visit on October 23.

stories.summary: Entretien «Le kadhafisme, c'est aussi le reflet d'une histoire et de bouleversements d'une société» Quinze ans après la mort de Mouammar Kadhafi, le 20 octobre 2011, que reste-t-il de son idéologie et de son héritage en Libye mais aussi au-delà de ses frontières ? Éléments d’analyse et de réflexion avec Virginie Collombier, docteure en sciences politiques, spécialiste de la Libye et cofondatrice de Mediterranean Platform. Virginie Collombier* : Le kadhafisme a été souvent perçu symboliquement à travers le Livre vert , mais ce n'est pas l'unique point de référence, c'est le texte doctrinal et idéologique central : une troisième voie qui pouvait servir d'alternative aux deux idéologies centrales au XXᵉ siècle, le capitalisme et le communisme.

stories.title: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing
stories.summary: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing Tim McKulka/UNMISS UN peacekeepers patrol the Abyei area (file photo) 19 October 2026 African Arguments analysis By Sergey Eledinov On 6 October, Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan said again that there would be no negotiations with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, or 'any other party' , and that the war would go on until victory. A day earlier, Donald Trump's envoy Massad Boulos had disclosed a meeting with him in Egypt . Washington is pushing a 90-day humanitarian truce and, according to sources cited by Reuters , made Burhan's visa for the UN General Assembly conditional on it. In 1996, General Alexander Lebed told the journalist Yevgeny Kiselyov on Russia's NTV that 'all wars, even hundred-year wars, end in negotiations and peace all the same'. He then asked whether it was worth piling up mountains of corpses only to sit down and negotiate anyway.

stories.title: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Wave of Drone Strikes in War-Torn Sudan
stories.summary: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Wave of Drone Strikes in War-Torn Sudan Stuart Price/UN UN peacekeepers on patrol in Abyei. 19 October 2026 UN News Service Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger. "We are alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes across the country that are killing civilians, including children, and that are disrupting essential services," UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric told journalists in New York. The rising use of armed drones during the war between rival militaries comes at a time when 20 million people face acute hunger, with a rising risk of famine in parts of Darfur and Greater Kordofan. Fighting erupted in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) - former allies who had jointly seized power in a 2021 coup. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines This latest escalation comes on the heels of a spate of deadly drone attacks last week . Bloody Monday On Monday alone, drone strikes injured at least 19 people in a busy market in Abyei and targeted several locations in the capital, Khartoum, including an area near the airport.

stories.summary: Tchad: le médiateur de la République appelle au calme après des affrontements dans le Tibesti Au Tchad, le médiateur de la République Saleh Kebzabo appelle au calme alors que la tension reste vive dans le Tibesti. stories.summary: En visite en Côte d'Ivoire, le Premier ministre sénégalais veut redynamiser le partenariat entre Dakar et Abidjan À l'occasion d'une visite d'amitié et de travail dans la capitale économique ivoirienne lundi 19 octobre, Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô a notamment rencontré son homologue Robert Beugré Mambé et le président ivoirien Alassane Ouattara. Publié le : 20/10/2026 - 05:07 1 min Temps de lecture Le Premier ministre sénégalais Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô était en visite à Abidjan, lundi 19 octobre. [illustration] © RFI Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre correspondante à Abidjan, Fanny Noaro-Kabré Le Premier ministre sénégalais, Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô, a effectué une visite d’amitié et de travail en Côte d'Ivoire destinée à renforcer le partenariat entre Dakar et Abidjan, lundi 19 octobre. Accompagné d’une délégation gouvernementale comprenant notamment les ministres sénégalais de l’Intérieur, du Commerce et de l’Agriculture, ce dernier a notamment participé à une séance de travail avec son homologue Robert Beugré Mambé avant de conclure son déplacement par un entretien avec le président ivoirien Alassane Ouattara . Selon lui, les échanges ont consisté, « pour l’essentiel, à passer en revue la cinquantaine d’accords conclus entre les deux pays depuis les années 1970 ». « Très peu sont appliqués de façon satisfaisante », a regretté Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô pour qui « le volume des échanges économiques et commerciaux [sénégalo-ivoiriens] - évalués autour de 250 milliards de francs CFA - demeure en deçà du potentiel entre les deux pays ». De son côté, la Côte d’Ivoire veut renforcer ses partenariats avec le Sénégal , notamment dans les secteurs de l'agriculture, de l'énergie et des politiques publiques, a expliqué le Premier ministre ivoirien Robert Beugré Mambé, qui a dit souhaiter y voir une « participation accrue du secteur privé ».

stories.title: Tchad: l'épidémie de dengue continue de progresser et met en lumière les fragilités du système de santé
stories.summary: Tchad: l'épidémie de dengue continue de progresser et met en lumière les fragilités du système de santé Alors que cinq provinces tchadiennes sont désormais officiellement touchées par la maladie qui a déjà fait huit morts pour plus de 3000 cas suspects recensés, celle-ci révèle aussi la faiblesse du nombre de lits de réanimation disponibles dans le pays ainsi que les problèmes d'approvisionnement de ses laboratoires en kits de dépistage. Publié le : 20/10/2026 - 05:06 2 min Temps de lecture L'épidémie de dengue qui sévit actuellement au Tchad jette une lumière crue sur la fragilité de son système de santé [illustration]. © Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula / RFI Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre correspondante à Ndjamena, Nadia Ben Mahfoudh L'épidémie de dengue qui touche le Tchad continue de progresser. Alors que cinq provinces du pays sont désormais officiellement touchées par la maladie qui vient s’ajouter à la flambée saisonnière de paludisme, celle-ci a déjà fait huit morts pour plus de 3 000 cas suspects recensés, dont 2 472 dans la seule province du Wadi Fira, selon le bilan fourni par Dicia Fitouin, coordinateur du Centre des opérations d’urgence de santé publique. Mais si ces chiffres sont inquiétants, c'est aussi parce qu'ils révèlent combien le système de santé tchadien demeure fragile face aux catastrophes sanitaires. Alors qu'à ses débuts, les symptômes de la dengue ressemblent à ceux du paludisme qui flambe lui aussi en cette fin de saison des pluies - courbatures généralisées, léthargie, grande fatigue, fièvres ou encore maux de tête intenses -, beaucoup de malades se soignent seuls. « Les gens passent directement dans les pharmacies, qui donnent des anti-paludéens », explique le docteur Bargo, médecin urgentiste et secrétaire général de l’Association de développement de la santé privée au Tchad.

stories.title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister By Basma El Atti Published 20 October 2026, 00:30 BST The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister. Mustafa Ramid, a former justice minister in an Islamist-led government, cited the saying earlier this month, in a lengthy Facebook post questioning whether a woman should hold the country's highest political office. He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men. Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy. Yet executive power remains in the hands of the 63-year-old monarch.

stories.title: South Africa: Mbeki Denies Secret Deals With Apartheid-Era Generals
stories.summary: South Africa: Mbeki Denies Secret Deals With Apartheid-Era Generals, Blames NPA for TRC Prosecution Delays @TrustAfrica Thabo Mbeki. 19 October 2026 Daily Maverick (Johannesburg) By Marianne Thamm At the Khampepe Commission, Thabo Mbeki rejects claims of political interference, explaining the ANC's amnesty bid and distinguishing presidential pardons from prosecution decisions. Former president Thabo Mbeki has told the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry into delayed Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) prosecutions that the only occasion he met former apartheid military and police generals was when they had approached the ANC, stating they would not apply for amnesty if then president FW de Klerk and his cabinet did not do so as well. On the first day of his much-anticipated appearance, the former president denied any secret meetings and testified that former generals approached him in 1996, while the TRC was in progress, to request a meeting with the ANC committee tasked with amnesty applications. TRC ROULETTE 'Bodyguard of lies' -- Mbeki denies political interference in TRC matters, blames NPA October 12, 2026 In response to this "grievance" of the former generals, Mbeki said the ANC had offered to approach De Klerk and his leadership colleagues to persuade them to appear. In the meantime, "to create moral leverage and lead by example, the ANC leadership decided to apply for collective amnesty for its own political leadership", he told the panel.

The projected shift comes after Kenya overtook Ethiopia as East Africa's largest economy in nominal US dollar terms, marking another change in the continent's economic rankings driven partly by exchange-rate movements rather than differences in real economic growth. The IMF's latest estimates place Ghana eighth among Africa's largest economies, ahead of Ethiopia in ninth place and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose economy is projected at US$122.28 billion. While Ghana's nominal GDP is expected to edge ahead of Ethiopia's, the two countries have markedly different growth forecasts. Ethiopia's economy is projected to expand by 9.2% in real terms in 2026, compared with Ghana's forecast growth of 5.7%.

stories.summary: Africa's Pooled Procurement Mechanism Seeks to Lower Medical Product Costs 15 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 15 October 2026 - The African Pooled Procurement Mechanism (APPM) has moved from its pilot phase to a fully-fledged continental programme, with eight African Union Member States having signed the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to participate in the initiative. Another 15 countries have expressed intent to join the initiative, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) is targeting all 55 African Union Member States to participate in the APPM. The announcement came at the conclusion of the third APPM Member States Consultative Workshop held in Addis Ababa, marking a shift from political commitment to implementation, in line with African Union directives. Established by an African Union Assembly decision in February 2024, the APPM is spearheaded by Africa CDC to strengthen collective purchasing of essential health products across the continent. By pooling demand from Member States, the APPM aims to improve access to affordable, quality-assured health products, strengthen supply security, reduce procurement costs and create predictable, sustainable markets for African manufacturers.
